# Proof run: tell a JiuwenSwarm agent the CC task directly (no web frontend)

13 Nov 2026, 13:32–13:46 UTC, on Satay. Task `factory-cc5e8585445c484ba4d5b5b0dd96c31c`. Outcome: **accept**, 3 turns, 13 min 10 s.

## How it was invoked

```sh
cd ~/projects/jiuwenswarm
.venv/bin/jiuwenswarm-factory ask "<instruction below>" --model gpt-6.1-sol --branch proof-ask-1
```

**Instruction:**

> Use engine.expert_streaming to apply demand fill to plain llama.cpp cf34d3113 on your owned branch. Integrate expert_fill together with its declared source prerequisites (mmap_advice, router_prefetch) with their runtime switches off, committing each component. Build the candidate exactly once with factory.builder. Then run exactly one screen lab run (lab_client) of that image under the frozen contract qwen36-quick-v1 with the expert_fill component environment, to check output identity against the frozen reference and that fill engages. Then finish with a report of the commits, image, screen result and engagement. Do not run ABBA comparisons, do not integrate other components, do not tune settings.

**Path the instruction takes:**
1. CLI (`jiuwenswarm/factory/cli.py ask`)
2. factory controller
3. JiuwenSwarm agent adapter
4. Codex app-server over stdio (pinned 0.163.0, model `gpt-6.1-sol`)
5. the CC runner (`jiuwenswarm.ccv2.agent_mcp`, an MCP server), exposing the factory capsules
6. builder and lab jobs on the shared host queue

No web frontend or server is involved.

## What happened (all from the factory store; see STORY.txt and PLAN.txt)

| Step | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Capsules read; applicability passes (read-only) | rev 1 |
| Three capsule components integrated as separate commits on the owned branch `proof-ask-1`: `133bdac08` mmap_advice, `679bd0e1e` router_prefetch, `885eec824` expert_fill | rev 2. All five declared patch sha256 values and forward checks verified. Tree `d63f6127…` is **identical** to the fill candidate of the 13 Nov recording, so the integration is reproducible. |
| Built once via `factory.builder` | build `3445e556`: 165 s, CUDA 12.6 sm_87 release → image `factory/llamacpp:proof-ask-1-expert-fill` `sha256:a15f04f0…`, admitted for jetson-orin |
| One screen via `factory.lab_client`, frozen contract `qwen36-quick-v1` | lab `bbc85611`: **stdout `cad62aa9…` equals the frozen reference**; correctness pass, evidence complete |
| Fill engaged | Fill active (threads=16, chunk_kib=2048, random=decode), decode random advice applied, 1240 fill calls, 6.59 GB read during decode, 566 ms/token demand wait |
| Decision | rev 5 `accept`: frozen correctness plus demand-fill engagement, as instructed |

**Work graph.** All 10 work nodes carry `engine_slice: expert_weight_readiness` and `contract:qwen36-quick-v1`. This is the first live task to use the ontology link added in `6d10c8c5`.

## Limits

- **Not a speed claim.** The screen's 898.36 ms/token is a single preliminary run, and no comparison was run.
- **Contract-level engagement 0/2.** These two checks are for the effective-config line and the fill thread names. The fill-only source has no patches 08/09, so they are not measured. Fill engagement was established by the component's own checks.
- **Operator-directed scope.** The instruction fixed the scope (which components, one build, one screen). The agent chose the commit order from the declared dependencies, verified the patches, and chose to accept on the evidence.

## Where the evidence is

- **Sanitized export:** `~/backup/proof-ask-1-evidence/` (14 MB). Credential pattern scan: no hits.
- **Task JSON:** `task.json`, generated from `jiuwenswarm/factory/tasks/direct.json`.

## Follow-up speed check (J-ASK1, operator-allowed 10 min of lab time)

This is one 1-round ABBA (plain, fill, fill, plain) on the frozen 32-token contract. It used the siminfeng `cc/abrun` harness through the shared queue as job `job-279d89e2`, from 14:02 to 14:08, about 6.5 min of lab time.

| Arm | Runs (ms/token) | Mean |
|---|---|---|
| plain `bare-cf34d311` | 972.59, 865.27 | 918.93 |
| fill `proof-ask-1-expert-fill` | 886.44, 812.60 | 849.52 |

- **Speed:** 7.6% less time per token (A/B ratio 1.0817, +8.2% throughput).
- **Gate: null.** The A/A noise was 11.7%, so the threshold is 23.4%. This one-round result is not a confirmed improvement.
- **Output:** identical (`cad62aa9…`) in all four runs.
- **Engagement:** fill checks 3/3 in both fill runs.
- **Contention:** `host_contention` false in all runs.
- **I/O:** decode read 0.20 vs 0.29 GiB/token.

**How this compares:**
- It is consistent with the recorded task's two null ABBAs (+7.66% and +11.99%).
- It does not change the confirmed headline, which is J-OM13 (fill plus predictive reads, 64 tokens, 15.5%).

Results are in siminfeng `experiments/jetson/OM/J-ASK1/` (commit `7cab011`).

# Grow an engine with counterbalanced A/B evidence

Adapted from siminfeng c2/skills/engine-ab-experiment/SKILL.md and c2/METHODS.md;
cc/abrun/gate.py is the performance gate, not historical experiment numbers.

1. State the mechanism hypothesis, uncertainty, expected evidence, and scope
   before integrating. Read the component's dependencies and source patches.
   Change one component per experiment; keep every other workload variable fixed.
2. Record source commit, patch hashes, build receipt and immutable image IDs.
   Build the bare engine first. Current best starts there. Apply dependencies in
   order in the owned source.branch, with one integration commit per component.
   Dependencies are source requirements, not evidence of benefit: if a dependency
   was reverted, explicitly test its addition again or report the dependent blocked.
3. Fix the contract's model, prompt, seed, context, offload and greedy argv.
   The operator must freeze the bare contract reference before scoring.
   Candidate engagement checks belong to component.yaml, never to the contract.
4. Prefer env-only arms in one admitted image when that isolates the variable.
   Otherwise use the admitted current-best and candidate images. Keep the base
   environment at its recorded best settings; override only the treatment.
   Pass component ID to lab_client.ab_submit; the Manager selects checks.
   Each image input is {tag, id, build_attempt_id}; both require build admission.
5. Submit one complete ABBA experiment through lab_client.ab_submit with
   base_image, candidate_image, base_env, candidate_env, rounds, component and
   idem_key. Contract comes from the task (optional explicit matching contract_id).
   The Manager queues one durable gpu job; the worker runs abrun without --submit.
   End the agent turn after submission. Read ab_status / ab_result next turn.
   No GPU/build/heavy CPU overlap. Inspect queue and external load evidence;
   contaminated timing is unscored, never a win.
6. Use printed eval_ms_per_token (lower is better), not rounded reciprocal t/s.
   ABBA provides repeated A/A and B/B observations; repeat complete rounds.
   Inspect all summaries, startup activation and exit counters, stdout hashes,
   telemetry, watchdog and REPORT.md. Success or an env string is not engagement.
   thread_names uses sampled xfill-* workers, has measure: none, and cannot
   establish a performance improvement on its own.
7. gate.py computes arithmetic arm means. For ms/token ratio is A/B.
   aa_gap is the largest within-arm (max-min)/mean. Drift is the absolute
   difference of the two base-half means divided by the whole base mean.
   threshold = max(0.03, 2 * aa_gap, 2 * (drift or 0.0)).
   Improvement requires ratio - 1 strictly above threshold; equality is null.
   Missing, nonpositive or nonfinite metrics, unsuccessful runs or activation
   mismatches invalidate scoring. Missing replication is not stability evidence.
8. Require output class identical AND every base stdout SHA equal to the frozen
   contract reference. Unknown or differing output is candidate_failed even if
   speed improves. Identical greedy stdout is this contract's obligation; it is
   not a general accuracy or numerical-equivalence claim.
9. Read ab_result: gate, ratio, aa_gap, output_class, per_arm_ms and evaluation.
   Read acceptance.type/verdict/reasons. Performance requires gate improved;
   observability requires every candidate engagement check passing, correctness
   pass, and overhead 1/ratio - 1 <= max(overhead_bound, gate threshold).
   thread_names is keepable on sampled signal plus bounded overhead; never claim
   a speed gain from it. Missing capture is not_measured and acceptance invalid.
   All keeps require valid complete evidence and correctness pass. Publish
   keep_component {component,image,ratio} citing ab_result acceptance.verdict
   accept and the evaluation. Otherwise revert with component and reason anytime,
   restore best env/image and retain the failed/null evidence.
   Exception, dormant prerequisite: if a rejected component's source is required
   by components not yet measured and its switch is off by default, you may keep
   its commit with the switch OFF in every later arm and publish keep_dormant
   {component,reason,needed_by}. Its own rejection still stands; dependents are
   measured against the current best with only their own switches on. If a
   dependent is later rejected too, revert both in reverse order.
10. Retain negative/null/invalid evidence and explain why. Finish with the best
    image, kept component stack, exact scope and evidence IDs. Budgets or missing
    prerequisites end inconclusively; they never imply a win.
11. To explain a result, not to score it, submit one lab_client.submit with
    run_config {"env": ..., "profile": "nsys"}. Nsight Systems traces the run;
    the evaluation carries details.nsys: top GPU kernels, CUDA API calls and
    OS-runtime calls (pread, futex, waits) with total times. Tracing slows the
    engine, so traced ms/token is never compared or cited as speed evidence.
    Use it to form the next hypothesis, then test that with an untraced A/B.

Never multiply successive component ratios. Final claim = direct bare-vs-final
ABBA if budget allows; otherwise explicitly state that comparison is not measured.
Settings trials: one knob, justified hypothesis, at most 3 trials per component.
Changing scoring rules requires a new contract id and a fresh reference.

# Expert-streaming evidence method

Separate load, prompt and decode before attributing cost. Decode is printed
`eval_ms_per_token`; fill stats provide distinct prompt_* and decode_* fields.
Whole-run copy/IO time is not automatically a decode bottleneck. Counters with
no phase split cannot silently be described as decode counters.

These claims are different and require different evidence:

- Predicted right: hits, actual and recall_at_k describe routing recall.
- Bytes ready before demand: readiness counters split predicted and unpredicted
  selected bytes, when the readiness component is present. hit_done is IO job
  state, not a residency probe; resident-at-predict is not credited to prediction.
- Fewer faults/bytes: per-phase fault counters and bytes read need their own
  comparison. pread can replace faults without reducing IO; duplicate and wasted
  reads matter. Missing blocks are not_measured, never zero.
- Lower decode ms/token: only the untraced contract-bound ABBA gate establishes
  this. Neither recall, readiness, lower faults nor whole-run copy time implies it.

Traced nsys and DIAG=1 runs explain mechanisms; they perturb timing. Score
untraced ABBA. Read engagement per arm/run and preserve raw stderr artifacts.
The tool reports decode-byte and decode-wait rates only with an actual decode
token denominator (readiness or printed eval tokens), not layer call counts.

## Acceptance by module

Performance components (expert_fill, expert_pregate, mmap_advice,
router_prefetch, later inflight_join) require gate improved, complete valid
measurements, passing engagement and byte-identical correctness.
Observability components (thread_names, later expert_readiness) require every
candidate engagement check to pass, correctness pass and candidate overhead
`1/ratio - 1 <= max(overhead_bound, gate threshold)` where ratio=A/B ms/token.
thread_names has overhead_bound=0.03; no speedup is required and never claim a
speed gain from names. Missing signal capture is invalid, not rejection evidence.
Prerequisite source may stay dormant only per AB.md step 9; it is not an enabled
performance win. Cite acceptance.verdict=accept for keep_component.

A failed/null idea remains useful knowledge. Preserve all raw evidence and
negative results. A change of scoring rules requires a new contract id and fresh
reference, never relabeling old results. Do not multiply successive ratios:
final speed claims require direct bare-vs-final ABBA if budget allows; otherwise
state that the final comparison is not measured.

## Page-cache state is a confound

The model file (20.8 GiB) is far larger than RAM, so how much of it is cached
when a run starts changes decode speed a lot (a run starting at 0% resident
measured 1290 ms/token where warm ABBA chains measured about 711; J-XS2-smoke vs
J-OM13). Read `page_cache.start.json` for every run, compare start residency
across arms, and state the protocol (carryover, cold, warm) with any claim. A
comparison across different protocols, or with very different start residency,
is not a valid speed comparison.

# Expert streaming into an existing llama.cpp

On UMA with mmap, selected experts' weight pages are read from the GGUF mapping
on demand. In stock llama.cpp the compute thread takes the page faults. This
capability targets MoE with CPU-side experts (`-cmoe`/`--cpu-moe` or CPU `-ot`
overrides), expert bytes much greater than available memory, and mmap loading.
Use applicability first: it reads only the model header and host memory. Its
2x memory heuristic is guidance, not a performance prediction; partial placement
and unknown mappings need inspection. Read SOURCE-MAP.md for source anchors.

This is not expert placement: CPU vs GPU residency, `--n-cpu-moe`, and `-ot`
are placement controls. No component here moves experts to the GPU.

## Choose a mechanism

- Demand-driven fill (`expert_fill`) reads selected nonresident ranges through
  parallel buffered reads before computation. Try this first when decode faults
  suggest demand IO; it has a direct engagement and decode-byte test.
- Predictive reads (`expert_pregate`) try upcoming expert routes and schedule
  asynchronous reads. Try only after understanding fill-only evidence; routing
  recall cannot establish that data arrived early enough.
- Supporting integration/observability: `mmap_advice` and `router_prefetch` are
  source prerequisites for fill. diag/observe explain faults and scheduling;
  `thread_names` (patch 09) names fill workers xfill-N so the lab's thread
  sampler can attribute them; it must be integrated before it can engage.
  `expert_readiness` (patch 10) measures, at each layer arrival and before demand
  fill, which selected bytes were already resident, split by predicted vs not,
  plus wasted speculative bytes and demand bytes that duplicated an in-flight
  read. `inflight_join` (patch 11, performance) removes those duplicate reads by
  waiting on the in-flight async read; its source needs patch 10, but readiness
  can stay switched off at run time.
  `phase_stats` (patch 16, observability) prints decode-only fault, context
  switch and CPU-time deltas plus per-token latency p50/p95/max, with fill on
  or off, so cost can be attributed without a perturbing trace.

Source dependency does not mean runtime enablement. A present patch's switch
stays off unless its own evidence supports it. Keep failed prerequisites dormant
only under AB.md step 9, recording needed_by and the off settings in every arm.

## Decide from evidence

Read EVIDENCE.md and factory.methodology_ab before integrating. Start with the
identified working engine and frozen reference; inspect effective configuration,
source dependencies, engagement, and load/prompt/decode separately. Fill not
engaged means check effective configuration before changing the mechanism.
High recall with low readiness suggests reads arrive too late (timing, queue
depth or device bandwidth) rather than wrong guesses; test which before acting.
Fewer faults with unchanged decode time means IO may not be the bottleneck;
inspect compute and critical-path waits before adding more IO. Whole-run IO or
copy time alone cannot locate decode cost. Missing readiness, per-phase faults,
critical-path matmul stalls or page-cache pressure limit attribution (see source
map). Stop or change direction when a bounded trial contradicts its hypothesis,
no discriminating measurement is available, or the budget/stop condition is met.
A failed or null idea is retained knowledge.

## Bounded settings trials

At most 3 settings trials per component. Publish a justified, falsifiable
hypothesis for each, vary one knob per trial, keep the workload fixed, and use
env-only untraced ABBA on an admitted image. Engine strict validation owns value
range checking: an abort is evidence. These are the component env_ranges (source
revision qualifications matter):

- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL`: 0|1
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_CHUNK_KIB`: 03: 1..65536, otherwise fallback 1024; 08: strict 64..65536
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_DIAG`: 0|1
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_DIAG_CSV`: nonempty path; optional; only used with diagnostics
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_MAX_TOKENS`: 04: unsigned integer, 0 unlimited; 08: 0..2147483647
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_MIN_TOKENS`: 04: unsigned integer, 0 unlimited; 08: 0..2147483647
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_POPULATE`: 0|1
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_RANDOM`: 0|1|decode (decode added by 04)
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_THREADS`: 03: 1..256, otherwise fallback 8; 08: strict 1..64
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH`: 1 enables; otherwise off (08: strict 0|1)
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH_NEXT`: 1 enables next-layer same-ID prediction; otherwise off (08: strict 0|1)
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_PREGATE`: 0|1
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_PREGATE_K`: 1..32
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_PREGATE_LOOKAHEAD`: 1..2
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_PREGATE_MAX_INFLIGHT`: 1..64 (also capped by fill threads)
- `LLAMA_EXPERT_PREGATE_ORDER`: after|before
- `LLAMA_MMAP_ADVICE`: random enables; any other value keeps default advice

## Name the engine target, then revise the work

For a new task, constraints.engine_slice = expert_weight_readiness links the
operator's engineering contract to the named domain slice in ONTOLOGY.yaml.
The host seeds that target and the scored contract reference onto work nodes.
Keep the target when revising relevant work; no task graph is an engine diagram.
Use the slice's regions to explain where the chosen component acts and its
quantities to name the discriminating observation. The engine ontology is a
small provisional vocabulary, not a complete inferred model of llama.cpp.

The existing decision loop is sufficient: inspect known evidence, state one
hypothesis and a deferred alternative, choose the minimum applicable component
set, build only changed source, screen correctness and engagement, and compare
only if the budget and screen justify it. Update the decision from the new
observations; continue, revert or report inconclusive. Never prescribe a fixed
number of improving versions. A single agent may consult this methodology,
factory.methodology_ab, factory.integration_skill and the builder/lab capsules
in one task. Guidance is read by the agent; it does not itself execute patches.

For the recovery/demo task, existing evidence is the default. Its six-hour total
and two-hour lab ceilings do not require consuming either budget. At most one
new candidate is justified only by a discriminating existing observation; do not
rerun simply to obtain a prettier number. Preserve all attempts and distinguish
recorded demonstrations, preliminary screens and scored comparisons.

diff --git a/src/llama-context.cpp b/src/llama-context.cpp
index a450d8257..cfdc0a257 100644
--- a/src/llama-context.cpp
+++ b/src/llama-context.cpp

 #include <string>
 #include <unordered_map>
 
+#ifdef __linux__
+#include <sys/mman.h>

+
 //
 // llama_context

@@ -636,10 +641,444 @@ llama_context::llama_context(
     }
 }
 
+#ifdef __linux__
+void llama_context::expert_fill_init() {
+    if (expert_fill_checked) { return; }
+    expert_fill_checked = true;
+    const char * fill = getenv("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL");
+    if (!fill || strcmp(fill, "1") != 0) { return; }
+    try {
+        for (const auto & layer : model.layers) {
+            for (const ggml_tensor * w : {layer.ffn_gate_exps, layer.ffn_up_exps, layer.ffn_down_exps, layer.ffn_gate_up_exps}) {
+                if (!w) { continue; }
+                llama_model::expert_file_range info;
+                if (w->ne[2] <= 0 || w->ne[3] != 1 || !ggml_is_contiguous(w) || !w->nb[2] ||
+                        !model.expert_file_info(w, info)) {
+                    throw std::runtime_error("expert tensors not mmap-backed or file offsets unavailable/unsupported layout");
+                }
+                if (!expert_fillers.count(info.file_index)) {
+                    expert_fillers.emplace(info.file_index, std::make_unique<ExpertFiller>(
+                        "/proc/self/fd/" + std::to_string(info.source_fd), info.mapping, info.mapping_size));
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        if (expert_fillers.empty()) { throw std::runtime_error("no mmap-backed expert tensors"); }
+        expert_prefetch_layers.resize(model.layers.size());
+        expert_fill_enabled = true;
+        expert_diag_enabled = expert_fillers.begin()->second->diagnostic();
+        if (expert_diag_enabled) {
+            const char * csv = getenv("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_DIAG_CSV");
+            if (csv && *csv) {
+                expert_diag_csv = fopen(csv, "w");
+                if (!expert_diag_csv) { throw std::runtime_error("cannot open diagnostic CSV"); }
+                fprintf(expert_diag_csv, "token_idx,fill_ns,between_ns,majflt_fill,majflt_between,post_fill_nonresident_pages,pre_use_nonresident_pages,bytes_read\n");
+            }
+        }
+        const char * random = getenv("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_RANDOM");
+        expert_fill_random_decode = random && strcmp(random, "decode") == 0;
+        auto token_limit = [](const char * name) -> uint64_t {
+            const char * value = getenv(name);
+            if (!value || !*value || *value == '-') { return 0; }
+            char * end = nullptr; errno = 0;
+            const auto n = strtoull(value, &end, 10);
+            return errno || *end ? 0 : n;
+        };
+        expert_fill_min_tokens = token_limit("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_MIN_TOKENS");
+        expert_fill_max_tokens = token_limit("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_MAX_TOKENS");
+        const auto & filler = *expert_fillers.begin()->second;
+        LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: active threads=%zu chunk_kib=%zu random=%s files=%zu\n",
+            filler.threads(), filler.chunk_bytes() / 1024, expert_fill_random_decode ? "decode" : (random && strcmp(random, "1") == 0 ? "1" : "0"), expert_fillers.size());
+    } catch (const std::exception & e) {
+        expert_fill_enabled = false; expert_diag_enabled = false;
+        if (expert_diag_csv) { fclose(expert_diag_csv); expert_diag_csv = nullptr; }
+        expert_fillers.clear();
+        LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: inactive (%s)\n", e.what());
+    }
+}
+
+static uint64_t expert_diag_now() {
+    return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
+        std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
+}
+void llama_context::expert_diag_close_gap() {
+    if (!expert_diag_gap) { return; }
+    struct rusage r {}; getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &r);
+    expert_diag_token.between_ns += expert_diag_now() - expert_diag_gap_ns;
+    expert_diag_token.majflt_between += r.ru_majflt - expert_diag_gap_maj;
+    expert_diag_token.minflt_between += r.ru_minflt - expert_diag_gap_min;
+    expert_diag_gap = false;
+}
+void llama_context::expert_diag_finish_token() {
+    if (!expert_diag_enabled || !expert_diag_token_active) { return; }
+    expert_diag_close_gap();
+    const auto & d = expert_diag_token;
+    expert_diag_total.fill_ns += d.fill_ns;

     // Callback while copying input weights of a split
     // if the user returns false the scheduler simply copies the entire weight
     // the callback is called only for input weights in host buffers

+#ifdef __linux__
+void llama_context::expert_fill_init() {
+    if (expert_fill_checked) { return; }
+    expert_fill_checked = true;
+    const char * fill = getenv("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL");
+    if (!fill || strcmp(fill, "1") != 0) { return; }
+    try {
+        for (const auto & layer : model.layers) {
+            for (const ggml_tensor * w : {layer.ffn_gate_exps, layer.ffn_up_exps, layer.ffn_down_exps, layer.ffn_gate_up_exps}) {
+                if (!w) { continue; }
+                llama_model::expert_file_range info;
+                if (w->ne[2] <= 0 || w->ne[3] != 1 || !ggml_is_contiguous(w) || !w->nb[2] ||
+                        !model.expert_file_info(w, info)) {
+                    throw std::runtime_error("expert tensors not mmap-backed or file offsets unavailable/unsupported layout");
+                }
+                if (!expert_fillers.count(info.file_index)) {
+                    expert_fillers.emplace(info.file_index, std::make_unique<ExpertFiller>(
+                        "/proc/self/fd/" + std::to_string(info.source_fd), info.mapping, info.mapping_size));
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        if (expert_fillers.empty()) { throw std::runtime_error("no mmap-backed expert tensors"); }
+        expert_prefetch_layers.resize(model.layers.size());
+        expert_fill_enabled = true;
+        expert_diag_enabled = expert_fillers.begin()->second->diagnostic();
+        if (expert_diag_enabled) {
+            const char * csv = getenv("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_DIAG_CSV");
+            if (csv && *csv) {
+                expert_diag_csv = fopen(csv, "w");
+                if (!expert_diag_csv) { throw std::runtime_error("cannot open diagnostic CSV"); }
+                fprintf(expert_diag_csv, "token_idx,fill_ns,between_ns,majflt_fill,majflt_between,post_fill_nonresident_pages,pre_use_nonresident_pages,bytes_read\n");
+            }
+        }
+        const char * random = getenv("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_RANDOM");
+        expert_fill_random_decode = random && strcmp(random, "decode") == 0;
+        auto token_limit = [](const char * name) -> uint64_t {
+            const char * value = getenv(name);
+            if (!value || !*value || *value == '-') { return 0; }
+            char * end = nullptr; errno = 0;
+            const auto n = strtoull(value, &end, 10);
+            return errno || *end ? 0 : n;
+        };
+        expert_fill_min_tokens = token_limit("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_MIN_TOKENS");
+        expert_fill_max_tokens = token_limit("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_MAX_TOKENS");
+        const auto & filler = *expert_fillers.begin()->second;
+        LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: active threads=%zu chunk_kib=%zu random=%s files=%zu\n",
+            filler.threads(), filler.chunk_bytes() / 1024, expert_fill_random_decode ? "decode" : (random && strcmp(random, "1") == 0 ? "1" : "0"), expert_fillers.size());
+    } catch (const std::exception & e) {
+        expert_fill_enabled = false; expert_diag_enabled = false;
+        if (expert_diag_csv) { fclose(expert_diag_csv); expert_diag_csv = nullptr; }
+        expert_fillers.clear();
+        LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: inactive (%s)\n", e.what());
+    }
+}
+
+static uint64_t expert_diag_now() {
+    return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
+        std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
+}
+void llama_context::expert_diag_close_gap() {
+    if (!expert_diag_gap) { return; }
+    struct rusage r {}; getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &r);
+    expert_diag_token.between_ns += expert_diag_now() - expert_diag_gap_ns;
+    expert_diag_token.majflt_between += r.ru_majflt - expert_diag_gap_maj;
+    expert_diag_token.minflt_between += r.ru_minflt - expert_diag_gap_min;
+    expert_diag_gap = false;
+}
+void llama_context::expert_diag_finish_token() {
+    if (!expert_diag_enabled || !expert_diag_token_active) { return; }
+    expert_diag_close_gap();
+    const auto & d = expert_diag_token;
+    expert_diag_total.fill_ns += d.fill_ns;
+    expert_diag_total.between_ns += d.between_ns;
+    expert_diag_total.majflt_fill += d.majflt_fill;
+    expert_diag_total.minflt_fill += d.minflt_fill;
+    expert_diag_total.majflt_between += d.majflt_between;
+    expert_diag_total.minflt_between += d.minflt_between;
+    expert_diag_total.thread_majflt += d.thread_majflt;
+    expert_diag_total.thread_minflt += d.thread_minflt;
+    expert_diag_total.post_nonresident += d.post_nonresident;
+    expert_diag_total.pre_use_nonresident += d.pre_use_nonresident;
+    expert_diag_total.next_nonresident += d.next_nonresident;
+    expert_diag_total.bytes_read += d.bytes_read;
+    expert_diag_total.post_checks += d.post_checks;
+    expert_diag_total.pre_use_checks += d.pre_use_checks;
+    expert_diag_total.next_checks += d.next_checks;
+    expert_diag_total.populate_calls += d.populate_calls;
+    expert_diag_total.populate_ns += d.populate_ns;
+    expert_diag_total.populate_errors += d.populate_errors;
+    if (expert_diag_csv) {
+        fprintf(expert_diag_csv, "%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu\n",
+            (unsigned long long)expert_diag_token_idx, (unsigned long long)d.fill_ns,
+            (unsigned long long)d.between_ns, (unsigned long long)d.majflt_fill,
+            (unsigned long long)d.majflt_between, (unsigned long long)d.post_nonresident,
+            (unsigned long long)d.pre_use_nonresident, (unsigned long long)d.bytes_read);
+        fflush(expert_diag_csv);
+    }
+    if (expert_diag_token_idx % 16 == 0) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "expert_fill: diag token=%llu fill_ns=%llu between_ns=%llu majflt_fill=%llu majflt_between=%llu post_nonresident=%llu pre_use_nonresident=%llu bytes_read=%llu\n",
+            (unsigned long long)expert_diag_token_idx, (unsigned long long)d.fill_ns,
+            (unsigned long long)d.between_ns, (unsigned long long)d.majflt_fill,
+            (unsigned long long)d.majflt_between, (unsigned long long)d.post_nonresident,
+            (unsigned long long)d.pre_use_nonresident, (unsigned long long)d.bytes_read);
+    }
+    expert_diag_token = {}; expert_diag_token_active = false;
+    expert_diag_layers.clear(); expert_diag_previous.clear();
+}
+void llama_context::expert_diag_pre_use(size_t il) {
+    if (!expert_diag_enabled || !expert_diag_token_active) { return; }
+    auto it = expert_diag_layers.find(il);
+    if (it == expert_diag_layers.end()) { return; }
+    for (const auto & entry : it->second) {
+        expert_diag_token.pre_use_nonresident += expert_fillers.at(entry.first)->nonresident(entry.second);
+        ++expert_diag_token.pre_use_checks;
+    }
+}
+void llama_context::expert_fill_phase(uint32_t n_tokens) {
+    if (expert_diag_enabled) {
+        expert_diag_finish_token();
+        if (n_tokens == 1) {
+            ++expert_diag_token_idx; expert_diag_token_active = true;
+            struct rusage r {}; getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &r);
+            expert_diag_gap_maj = r.ru_majflt; expert_diag_gap_min = r.ru_minflt;
+            expert_diag_gap_ns = expert_diag_now(); expert_diag_gap = true;
+        }
+    }
+    expert_fill_decode = n_tokens == 1;
+    expert_fill_this_ubatch = n_tokens >= expert_fill_min_tokens &&
+        (!expert_fill_max_tokens || n_tokens <= expert_fill_max_tokens);
+    if (!expert_fill_enabled || expert_fill_failed || !expert_fill_random_decode ||
+            expert_fill_random_applied || !expert_fill_decode) { return; }
+    // Transition before the first single-token graph, including when fill is filtered out.
+    expert_fill_random_applied = true;
+    const long page = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
+    bool ok = page > 0;
+    for (const auto & layer : model.layers) {
+        for (const ggml_tensor * w : {layer.ffn_gate_exps, layer.ffn_up_exps, layer.ffn_down_exps, layer.ffn_gate_up_exps}) {
+            if (!w) { continue; }
+            llama_model::expert_file_range info;
+            if (!ok || !model.expert_file_info(w, info)) { ok = false; continue; }
+            const size_t first = info.offset - info.offset % size_t(page);
+            const size_t end = info.offset + ggml_nbytes(w);
+            const size_t pad = (size_t(page) - end % size_t(page)) % size_t(page);
+            const size_t last = end + std::min(pad, info.mapping_size - end);
+            if (madvise(static_cast<char *>(info.mapping) + first, last - first, MADV_RANDOM)) { ok = false; }
+        }
+    }
+    if (ok) {
+        LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: random advice applied at decode\n");
+    } else {
+        expert_fill_failed = true;
+        LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: inactive (decode random advice failed)\n");
+    }
+}
+
+void llama_context::expert_fill_selected(size_t il, const std::vector<int32_t> & selected) {
+    if (expert_fill_failed || !expert_fill_this_ubatch) { return; }
+    try {
+        std::map<size_t, std::vector<ExpertFiller::Range>> ranges;
+        const auto & layer = model.layers[il];
+        for (const ggml_tensor * w : {layer.ffn_gate_exps, layer.ffn_up_exps, layer.ffn_down_exps, layer.ffn_gate_up_exps}) {
+            if (!w) { continue; }
+            llama_model::expert_file_range info;
+            if (!model.expert_file_info(w, info)) { throw std::runtime_error("expert mmap/file offsets unavailable"); }
+            for (const auto id : selected) {
+                if (id < 0 || id >= w->ne[2] || size_t(id) > (SIZE_MAX - info.offset) / w->nb[2]) {
+                    throw std::runtime_error("expert slice out of bounds");
+                }
+                ranges[info.file_index].push_back({info.offset + size_t(id) * w->nb[2], w->nb[2]});
+            }
+        }
+        const bool diag = expert_diag_enabled && expert_diag_token_active;
+        struct rusage before {}, after {}, thread_before {}, thread_after {};
+        uint64_t start = 0;
+        if (diag) {
+            // Previous layer was consumed; this is a separate, after-use eviction probe.
+            for (const auto & entry : expert_diag_previous) {
+                expert_diag_token.next_nonresident += expert_fillers.at(entry.first)->nonresident(entry.second);
+                ++expert_diag_token.next_checks;
+            }
+            expert_diag_close_gap();
+            getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &before); getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD, &thread_before);
+            start = expert_diag_now();
+        }
+        for (const auto & entry : ranges) {
+            auto & filler = *expert_fillers.at(entry.first);
+            ExpertFiller::Counters a {};
+            if (diag) { a = filler.counters(); }
+            filler.fill(entry.second, expert_fill_decode);
+            if (diag) {
+                const auto b = filler.counters();
+                expert_diag_token.bytes_read += b.bytes_read - a.bytes_read;
+                expert_diag_token.thread_majflt += b.thread_majflt - a.thread_majflt;
+                expert_diag_token.thread_minflt += b.thread_minflt - a.thread_minflt;
+                expert_diag_token.populate_calls += b.populate_calls - a.populate_calls;
+                expert_diag_token.populate_ns += b.populate_ns - a.populate_ns;
+                expert_diag_token.populate_errors += b.populate_errors - a.populate_errors;
+                expert_diag_token.post_nonresident += filler.nonresident(entry.second);
+                ++expert_diag_token.post_checks;
+            }
+        }
+        if (diag) {
+            getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &after); getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD, &thread_after);
+            expert_diag_token.fill_ns += expert_diag_now() - start;
+            expert_diag_token.majflt_fill += after.ru_majflt - before.ru_majflt;
+            expert_diag_token.minflt_fill += after.ru_minflt - before.ru_minflt;
+            expert_diag_token.thread_majflt += thread_after.ru_majflt - thread_before.ru_majflt;
+            expert_diag_token.thread_minflt += thread_after.ru_minflt - thread_before.ru_minflt;
+            expert_diag_layers[il] = ranges; expert_diag_previous = ranges;
+            getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &after);
+            expert_diag_gap_maj = after.ru_majflt; expert_diag_gap_min = after.ru_minflt;
+            expert_diag_gap_ns = expert_diag_now(); expert_diag_gap = true;
+        }
+    } catch (const std::exception & e) {
+        expert_fill_failed = true;
+        LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: inactive (%s)\n", e.what());
+    }
+}
+#endif
+
+void llama_context::expert_prefetch_advise(size_t il, int32_t id) {
+#ifdef __linux__
+    auto & state = expert_prefetch_layers[il];
+    for (auto it = state.recent.begin(); it != state.recent.end();) {
+        if (state.tokens - it->second >= 32) {
+            it = state.recent.erase(it);
+        } else {
+            if (it->first == id) {
+                const auto hit = *it;
+                state.recent.erase(it);
+                state.recent.push_back(hit);
+                return;
+            }
+            ++it;
+        }
+    }
+    const auto & layer = model.layers[il];
+    bool advised = false;
+    bool failed = false;
+    for (const ggml_tensor * w : { layer.ffn_gate_exps, layer.ffn_up_exps, layer.ffn_down_exps, layer.ffn_gate_up_exps }) {
+        if (!w) {
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (id < 0 || id >= w->ne[2] || w->ne[3] != 1 || !ggml_is_contiguous(w) ||
+                w->nb[2] == 0 || !model.tensor_is_mapped(w)) {
+            if (!expert_prefetch_warned) {
+                LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_prefetch: skipping non-mmap or non-expert-contiguous tensors/invalid ids (once)\n");
+                expert_prefetch_warned = true;
+            }
+            continue;
+        }
+        static const uintptr_t page = (uintptr_t) sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
+        const uintptr_t start = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(w->data) + size_t(id) * w->nb[2];
+        if (page == 0 || page == UINTPTR_MAX || start > UINTPTR_MAX - w->nb[2] ||
+                start + w->nb[2] > UINTPTR_MAX - (page - 1)) {
+            continue;
+        }
+        const uintptr_t first = start - start % page;
+        const uintptr_t end = start + w->nb[2];
+        const uintptr_t last = end + (page - end % page) % page;
+        ++expert_prefetch_calls;
+        expert_prefetch_bytes += last - first;
+        if (madvise(reinterpret_cast<void *>(first), last - first, MADV_WILLNEED) != 0) {
+            ++expert_prefetch_failures;
+            failed = true;
+        } else {
+            advised = true;
+        }
+    }
+    if (advised && !failed) {
+        if (state.recent.size() == 32) {
+            state.recent.erase(state.recent.begin());
+        }
+        state.recent.emplace_back(id, state.tokens);
+    }
+#else
+    (void) il;
+    (void) id;
+#endif
+}
+
+void llama_context::expert_prefetch_cb(ggml_tensor * t, bool ask, bool * observe, void * data) {
+    auto & ctx = *static_cast<llama_context *>(data);
+#ifdef __linux__
+    if (ctx.expert_fill_failed) { return; }
+#endif
+    if (t->op != GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID || !t->src[0] || !t->src[2]) {
+        return;
+    }
+    size_t il = 0;
+    for (; il < ctx.model.layers.size(); ++il) {
+        const auto & layer = ctx.model.layers[il];
+        if (t->src[0] == layer.ffn_up_exps || t->src[0] == layer.ffn_gate_exps ||
+                t->src[0] == layer.ffn_down_exps || t->src[0] == layer.ffn_gate_up_exps) {
+            break;
+        }
+    }
+#ifdef __linux__
+    if (il < ctx.model.layers.size() && ctx.expert_diag_enabled && ctx.expert_diag_token_active &&
+            ctx.expert_prefetch_layers[il].observed) {
+        *observe = true;
+        if (!ask) { ctx.expert_diag_pre_use(il); }
+        return;
+    }
+#endif
+    if (il == ctx.model.layers.size() || ctx.expert_prefetch_layers[il].observed) {
+        return;
+    }
+    *observe = true;
+    if (ask) {
+        return;
+    }
+    auto & state = ctx.expert_prefetch_layers[il];
+    state.observed = true;
+    const ggml_tensor * ids = t->src[2];
+    const ggml_tensor * base = ids->view_src ? ids->view_src : ids;
+    if (ids->type != GGML_TYPE_I32 || ids->ne[2] != 1 || ids->ne[3] != 1 ||
+            !ids->data || !base->buffer || !ggml_backend_buffer_is_host(base->buffer) ||
+            !strstr(ids->name, "ffn_moe_topk-")) {
+        if (!ctx.expert_prefetch_warned) {
+#ifdef __linux__
+            if (ctx.expert_fill_enabled) {
+                ctx.expert_fill_failed = true;
+                LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: inactive (unsupported host router ids)\n");
+            } else
+#endif
+            LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_prefetch: skipping unsupported router ids (once)\n");
+            ctx.expert_prefetch_warned = true;
+        }
+        return;
+    }
+    std::vector<int32_t> selected;
+    for (int64_t token = 0; token < ids->ne[1]; ++token) {
+        for (int64_t k = 0; k < ids->ne[0]; ++k) {
+            int32_t id;
+            memcpy(&id, static_cast<const char *>(ids->data) + token * ids->nb[1] + k * ids->nb[0], sizeof(id));
+            if (id >= 0 && id < t->src[0]->ne[2] &&
+                    std::find(selected.begin(), selected.end(), id) == selected.end()) {
+                selected.push_back(id);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+#ifdef __linux__
+    if (ctx.expert_fill_enabled) {
+        ctx.expert_fill_selected(il, selected);
+        if (ctx.expert_diag_enabled) { ctx.expert_diag_pre_use(il); }
+        return;
+    }
+#endif
+    state.tokens += ids->ne[1];
+    for (int32_t id : state.predicted) {
+        ++ctx.expert_prefetch_total;
+        ctx.expert_prefetch_hits += std::find(selected.begin(), selected.end(), id) != selected.end();
+    }
+    state.predicted.clear();
+    for (int32_t id : selected) {
+        ctx.expert_prefetch_advise(il, id);
+    }
+    if (ctx.expert_prefetch_next && il + 1 < ctx.model.layers.size()) {
+        auto & next = ctx.expert_prefetch_layers[il + 1];
+        const ggml_tensor * w = ctx.model.layers[il + 1].ffn_down_exps;
+        if (w && !next.observed) {
+            for (int32_t id : selected) {
+                if (id < w->ne[2]) {
+                    next.predicted.push_back(id);
+                    ctx.expert_prefetch_advise(il + 1, id);
+                }
+            }

diff --git a/src/llama-expert-fill.h b/src/llama-expert-fill.h
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..f3a264819
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/llama-expert-fill.h
@@ -0,0 +1,261 @@
+#pragma once
+// Linux buffered reads populate the same page cache as the model mmap.
+#include <algorithm>
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <sys/resource.h>
+#ifndef MADV_POPULATE_READ
+#define MADV_POPULATE_READ 22
+#endif
+#include <cerrno>
+#include <chrono>
+#include <condition_variable>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <exception>
+#include <fcntl.h>
+#include <limits>
+#include <mutex>
+#include <stdexcept>
+#include <string>
+#include <sys/mman.h>
+#include <sys/stat.h>
+#include <thread>
+#include <unistd.h>
+#include <vector>
+
+class ExpertFiller {
+public:
+    struct Range { uint64_t offset; size_t len; };
+    struct Counters {
+        uint64_t populate_calls = 0, populate_ns = 0, populate_errors = 0;
+        uint64_t thread_majflt = 0, thread_minflt = 0;
+        uint64_t calls = 0, ranges = 0, bytes_requested = 0;
+        uint64_t bytes_skipped_resident = 0, bytes_read = 0, read_syscalls = 0;
+        uint64_t total_fill_wall_ns = 0, max_single_fill_ns = 0;
+        uint64_t prompt_calls = 0, prompt_bytes_read = 0, prompt_fill_wall_ns = 0;
+        uint64_t decode_calls = 0, decode_bytes_read = 0, decode_fill_wall_ns = 0;
+    };
+    // mapping must be a live, offset-zero file mmap for the lifetime of this object.
+    ExpertFiller(const std::string & path, void * mapping, size_t mapping_size)
+        : mapping_(static_cast<char *>(mapping)), size_(mapping_size),
+          threads_(env_size("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_THREADS", 8, 256)),
+          chunk_(env_size("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_CHUNK_KIB", 1024, 65536) * 1024) {
+        diag_ = enabled("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_DIAG");
+        populate_ = enabled("LLAMA_EXPERT_FILL_POPULATE");
+        const long page = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
+        if (page <= 0 || !mapping_ || reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(mapping_) % page || !size_) {
+            throw std::runtime_error("invalid expert mmap");
+        }
+        page_ = size_t(page);
+        fd_ = open(path.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC);
+        if (fd_ < 0) { throw std::runtime_error("open expert file failed"); }
+        struct stat st {};
+        if (fstat(fd_, &st) || st.st_size < 0 || uint64_t(st.st_size) != size_) {
+            close(fd_); fd_ = -1;
+            throw std::runtime_error("expert file size differs from mmap");
+        }
+        try {
+            // Allocate before starting workers, so allocation failures cannot kill a worker.
+            scratch_.resize(threads_);
+            for (auto & b : scratch_) { b.resize(chunk_); }
+            for (size_t i = 0; i < threads_; ++i) { workers_.emplace_back([this, i] { worker(i); }); }
+        } catch (...) {
+            stop(); close(fd_); throw;
+        }
+    }
+    ~ExpertFiller() { stop(); if (fd_ >= 0) { close(fd_); } }
+    ExpertFiller(const ExpertFiller &) = delete;
+    ExpertFiller & operator=(const ExpertFiller &) = delete;
+    size_t threads() const { return threads_; }
+    size_t chunk_bytes() const { return chunk_; }
+    Counters counters() const { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(fill_mutex_); return counters_; }
+
+    bool diagnostic() const { return diag_; }
+    // Called only under the opt-in diagnostic guard. Counts page cache residency,
+    // not installed PTEs; errors are explicit rather than counted as residency.
+    uint64_t nonresident(const std::vector<Range> & ranges) const {
+        uint64_t count = 0;
+        std::vector<Range> sorted = ranges;
+        std::sort(sorted.begin(), sorted.end(), [](const Range & a, const Range & b) { return a.offset < b.offset; });
+        uint64_t checked_end = 0;
+        for (const auto & r : sorted) {
+            if (!r.len) { continue; }
+            const size_t first = std::max<uint64_t>(r.offset / page_ * page_, checked_end);
+            if (r.offset + r.len <= first) { continue; }
+            const size_t len = r.offset + r.len - first;
+            checked_end = first + ((len + page_ - 1) / page_) * page_;
+            std::vector<unsigned char> v((len + page_ - 1) / page_);
+            if (mincore(mapping_ + first, len, v.data())) { throw std::runtime_error("diag mincore failed"); }
+            for (auto b : v) { count += !(b & 1); }
+        }
+        return count;
+    }
+    void fill(const std::vector<Range> & ranges, bool decode = false) {
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> serial(fill_mutex_);
+        const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+        batch_diag_ = diag_ && decode;
+        ++counters_.calls;
+        ++(decode ? counters_.decode_calls : counters_.prompt_calls);
+        const uint64_t bytes_before = counters_.bytes_read;
+        counters_.ranges += ranges.size();
+        auto finish = [&] {
+            const uint64_t ns = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
+                std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
+            counters_.total_fill_wall_ns += ns;
+            (decode ? counters_.decode_fill_wall_ns : counters_.prompt_fill_wall_ns) += ns;
+            (decode ? counters_.decode_bytes_read : counters_.prompt_bytes_read) += counters_.bytes_read - bytes_before;
+            counters_.max_single_fill_ns = std::max(counters_.max_single_fill_ns, ns);
+        };
+        try {
+            std::vector<Range> aligned;
+            for (const auto & r : ranges) {
+                if (r.offset > size_ || r.len > size_ - r.offset) { throw std::out_of_range("expert range outside mmap"); }
+                if (!r.len) { continue; }
+                const uint64_t first = r.offset - r.offset % page_;
+                const uint64_t end = r.offset + r.len;
+                const size_t pad = (page_ - end % page_) % page_;
+                const uint64_t last = end + std::min<uint64_t>(pad, size_ - end);
+                aligned.push_back({first, size_t(last - first)});
+            }
+            std::sort(aligned.begin(), aligned.end(), [](const Range & a, const Range & b) { return a.offset < b.offset; });
+            std::vector<Range> merged;
+            for (const auto & r : aligned) {
+                if (!merged.empty() && r.offset <= merged.back().offset + merged.back().len) {
+                    auto & b = merged.back();
+                    b.len = size_t(std::max(b.offset + b.len, r.offset + r.len) - b.offset);
+                } else { merged.push_back(r); }
+            }
+            std::vector<Range> jobs;
+            for (const auto & r : merged) {
+                counters_.bytes_requested += r.len; // page-aligned union, once per fill
+                const size_t pages = r.len / page_ + (r.len % page_ != 0);
+                std::vector<unsigned char> resident(pages);
+                if (mincore(mapping_ + r.offset, r.len, resident.data())) { throw std::runtime_error("expert mincore failed"); }
+                size_t run = 0;
+                while (run < pages) {
+                    if (resident[run] & 1) {
+                        counters_.bytes_skipped_resident += std::min(page_, r.len - run * page_);
+                        ++run; continue;
+                    }
+                    const size_t first = run++;
+                    while (run < pages && !(resident[run] & 1)) { ++run; }
+                    const size_t end = std::min(r.len, run * page_);
+                    for (size_t pos = first * page_; pos < end;) {
+                        const size_t len = std::min(chunk_, end - pos);
+                        jobs.push_back({r.offset + pos, len}); pos += len;
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            {
+                std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
+                populating_ = false;
+                jobs_ = std::move(jobs); next_ = 0; pending_ = jobs_.size(); error_ = 0;
+                ready_.notify_all();
+                done_.wait(lock, [this] { return pending_ == 0; });
+                counters_.bytes_read += batch_bytes_; counters_.read_syscalls += batch_syscalls_;
+                batch_bytes_ = batch_syscalls_ = 0;
+                if (error_) { throw std::runtime_error("expert pread failed: errno=" + std::to_string(error_)); }
+                // All preads finish before populate, including ranges already resident.
+                if (populate_.load() && !populate_unsupported().load()) {
+                    jobs_.clear();
+                    for (const auto & r : merged) {
+                        for (size_t pos = 0; pos < r.len;) {
+                            const size_t populate_chunk = std::max(page_, chunk_ / page_ * page_);
+                            const size_t len = std::min(populate_chunk, r.len - pos);
+                            jobs_.push_back({r.offset + pos, len}); pos += len;
+                        }
+                    }
+                    populating_ = true; next_ = 0; pending_ = jobs_.size();
+                    ready_.notify_all();
+                    done_.wait(lock, [this] { return pending_ == 0; });
+                    if (error_) { throw std::runtime_error("expert populate failed: errno=" + std::to_string(error_)); }
+                }
+            }
+        } catch (...) { finish(); throw; }
+        finish();
+    }
+private:
+    static std::atomic<bool> & populate_unsupported() {
+        static std::atomic<bool> value {false}; return value;
+    }
+    static bool enabled(const char * name) {
+        const char * s = getenv(name); return s && std::string(s) == "1";
+    }
+    static size_t env_size(const char * name, size_t fallback, size_t maximum) {
+        const char * s = getenv(name);
+        if (!s || !*s || *s == '-') { return fallback; }
+        char * end = nullptr; errno = 0;
+        const auto n = strtoull(s, &end, 10);
+        return errno || *end || n == 0 || n > maximum ? fallback : size_t(n);
+    }
+    void stop() {
+        { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_); stopping_ = true; }
+        ready_.notify_all();
+        for (auto & t : workers_) { t.join(); }
+    }
+    void worker(size_t index) {
+        for (;;) {
+            Range job {};
+            {
+                std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
+                ready_.wait(lock, [this] { return stopping_ || next_ < jobs_.size(); });
+                if (stopping_) { return; }
+                job = jobs_[next_++];
+            }
+            size_t bytes = 0; uint64_t syscalls = 0; int error = 0;
+            struct rusage before {}, after {};
+            if (batch_diag_) { getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD, &before); }
+            uint64_t populate_ns = 0, populate_calls = 0, populate_errors = 0;
+            if (populating_) {
+                if (populate_.load() && !populate_unsupported().load()) {
+                    const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+                    ++populate_calls;
+                    if (madvise(mapping_ + job.offset, job.len, MADV_POPULATE_READ)) {
+                        ++populate_errors;
+                        if (errno == EINVAL) {
+                            populate_.store(false);
+                            if (!populate_unsupported().exchange(true)) { fprintf(stderr, "expert_fill: populate unsupported\n"); }
+                        } else { error = errno; }
+                    }
+                    populate_ns = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
+                        std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
+                }
+            } else while (bytes < job.len) {
+                ++syscalls;
+                const ssize_t n = pread(fd_, scratch_[index].data() + bytes, job.len - bytes, off_t(job.offset + bytes));
+                if (n < 0 && errno == EINTR) { continue; }
+                if (n <= 0) { error = n < 0 ? errno : EIO; break; }
+                bytes += size_t(n);
+            }
+            if (batch_diag_) { getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD, &after); }
+            {
+                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
+                counters_.populate_calls += populate_calls; counters_.populate_ns += populate_ns;
+                counters_.populate_errors += populate_errors;
+                if (batch_diag_) {
+                    counters_.thread_majflt += after.ru_majflt - before.ru_majflt;
+                    counters_.thread_minflt += after.ru_minflt - before.ru_minflt;
+                }
+                batch_bytes_ += bytes; batch_syscalls_ += syscalls;
+                if (error && !error_) { error_ = error; }
+                if (--pending_ == 0) { done_.notify_one(); }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    int fd_ = -1;
+    char * mapping_;
+    size_t size_, threads_, chunk_, page_ = 0;
+    mutable std::mutex fill_mutex_;
+    std::mutex mutex_;
+    std::condition_variable ready_, done_;
+    std::vector<std::thread> workers_;
+    std::vector<std::vector<char>> scratch_;
+    std::vector<Range> jobs_;
+    size_t next_ = 0, pending_ = 0;
+    bool stopping_ = false, diag_ = false, batch_diag_ = false, populating_ = false;
+    std::atomic<bool> populate_ {false};
+    int error_ = 0;
+    uint64_t batch_bytes_ = 0, batch_syscalls_ = 0;
+    Counters counters_;
+};

+            }

+bool llama_model::expert_file_info(const ggml_tensor * t, expert_file_range & out) const {
+    if (!t || !tensor_is_mapped(t)) { return false; }
+    const auto it = pimpl->expert_offsets.find(t->name);
+    if (it == pimpl->expert_offsets.end()) { return false; }
+    const auto idx = it->second.first;
+    const auto offset = it->second.second;
+    if (idx >= pimpl->mappings.size() || idx >= pimpl->expert_files.size()) { return false; }
+    const auto & mapping = pimpl->mappings[idx];
+    if (offset > mapping->size() || ggml_nbytes(t) > mapping->size() - offset ||
+            static_cast<char *>(mapping->addr()) + offset != t->data) { return false; }
+    out = {idx, offset, mapping->size(), mapping->addr(), pimpl->expert_files[idx]->file_id()};
+    return true;
+}
+
+bool llama_model::tensor_is_mapped(const ggml_tensor * t) const {
+    if (!t || !t->data) {
+        return false;
+    }
+    const uintptr_t ptr = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(t->data);
+    const size_t bytes = ggml_nbytes(t);
+    for (const auto & mapping : pimpl->mappings) {
+        const uintptr_t base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(mapping->addr());
+        if (ptr >= base && ptr - base <= mapping->size() && bytes <= mapping->size() - (ptr - base)) {
+            return true;
+        }
+    }
+    return false;
+}
+
 bool llama_model::no_alloc() const {
     return params.no_alloc;
 }

- **LIVE**: captured 13 Nov, 15:49–15:52 UTC, for this bundle.
- **HIST**: historical execution records.
- **SRC**: source inspection.

**Run 5 (task `53db4945`) is excluded throughout.**

(12 tokens, greedy). The capture prints the image ID, build info, prompt and command first. Replay with `scriptreplay -t 1-plain.timing 1-plain.typescript`. ## Attribution rules for the edit

- **The 15.5% belongs only to J-OM13 / image `1274abb8`.** The live engine `a15f04f0` is fill-only and has no confirmed speed result: J-ASK1 was null.
- **Show what the live pair actually shows:** same request, same answer, both engines ran. It is functionality only.
- **The fill-only recorded demo task `e5b8d4b7` was inconclusive** and is not in this bundle.
- The operator set the scope of the `ask` instruction (which components, one build, one screen). The agent chose the commit order, verified the patches, and decided to accept.

## Suggested segments (no narration or music; static items 5–10 s)

1. Live plain request and answer (`live/1-plain`). Keep the real timing, or label any compression.
2. `02-capsule`: the `expert_fill` component and the `STREAMING.md` mechanism.
3. `03-source`: diffstat, then the hook excerpt.
4. `04-builder`: receipt `image_id`, `succeeded`.
5. Live CC-engine request and identical answer (`live/2-cc-engine`).
6. `05-correctness`: output equals the frozen reference. Then `06`: J-OM13, labelled as a different, fill-plus-predictive-reads image built by agent task `bd173c08`.

#!/bin/bash
# Usage: run_engine.sh <image> [env flags...]  -- one-shot live request, 12 output tokens
IMG=$1; shift

      idem_key: text

    gives:

      jobq_id: json

    needs:

    kind: tool

      task_id: text

      ended: json

      resources: json

      result_refs: json

      cleanup_state: text

      history: json

    needs:

    changes:

    - process.exec

  cancel:

    kind: tool

    takes:

      attempt_id: text

    gives:

      attempt_id: text

      task_id: text

      kind: text

      idem_key: text

      fingerprint: text

      request: json

      state: text

      jobq_id: json

      owner: json

      started: json

      resources: json

      result_refs: json

      cleanup_state: text

      history: json

    needs:

    - python

    changes:

    - process.exec

  result:

    kind: tool

    does: Read build result references; submission alone is not success.

    takes:

      attempt_id: text

    gives:

      attempt_id: text

      state: text

      result_refs: json

    needs:

    - python

    changes:

    - process.exec

+#ifdef __linux__

+void llama_context::expert_fill_init() {

+    if (expert_fill_checked) { return; }

+    expert_fill_checked = true;

+    if (!expert_config.fill) { return; }

+    try {

+        for (const auto & layer : model.layers) {

+            for (const ggml_tensor * w : {layer.ffn_gate_exps, layer.ffn_up_exps, layer.ffn_down_exps, layer.ffn_gate_up_exps}) {

+                if (!w) { continue; }

+                llama_model::expert_file_range info;

+                if (w->ne[2] <= 0 || w->ne[3] != 1 || !ggml_is_contiguous(w) || !w->nb[2] ||

+                        !model.expert_file_info(w, info)) {

+                    throw std::runtime_error("expert tensors not mmap-backed or file offsets unavailable/unsupported layout");

+                }

+                if (!expert_fillers.count(info.file_index)) {

+                    expert_fillers.emplace(info.file_index, std::make_unique<ExpertFiller>(

+                        "/proc/self/fd/" + std::to_string(info.source_fd), info.mapping, info.mapping_size, expert_config));

+                }

+            }

+        }

+        if (expert_fillers.empty()) { throw std::runtime_error("no mmap-backed expert tensors"); }

+        expert_prefetch_layers.resize(model.layers.size());

+        expert_fill_enabled = true;

+        expert_pregate_init();

+        expert_diag_enabled = expert_fillers.begin()->second->diagnostic();

+        if (expert_diag_enabled) {

+            if (!expert_config.diag_csv.empty()) {

+                expert_diag_csv = fopen(expert_config.diag_csv.c_str(), "w");

+                if (!expert_diag_csv) { throw std::runtime_error("cannot open diagnostic CSV"); }

+                fprintf(expert_diag_csv, "token_idx,fill_ns,between_ns,majflt_fill,majflt_between,post_fill_nonresident_pages,pre_use_nonresident_pages,bytes_read\n");

+            }

+        }

+        expert_fill_random_decode = expert_config.random == "decode";

+        expert_fill_min_tokens = expert_config.min_tokens;

+        expert_fill_max_tokens = expert_config.max_tokens;

+        const auto & filler = *expert_fillers.begin()->second;

+        LLAMA_LOG_INFO("expert_fill: active threads=%zu chunk_kib=%zu random=%s files=%zu\n",

+            filler.threads(), filler.chunk_bytes() / 1024, expert_config.random.c_str(), expert_fillers.size());

+    } catch (const std::exception & e) {

+        expert_fill_enabled = false; expert_diag_enabled = false;

+        if (expert_diag_csv) { fclose(expert_diag_csv); expert_diag_csv = nullptr; }

+        expert_fillers.clear();
